chunks: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever swears an oath in secret, let him make his exception in secret; and whoever swears an oath publicly, let him make his exception publicly.'
ai.seo_question: How should one make an exception to an oath depending on whether it was sworn privately or publicly?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural integrity of *istithna'* (exception) in oaths, ensuring that the public or private nature of the vow is mirrored in its revocation to maintain legal and social consistency. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction prevents ambiguity in the validity of the oath's nullification, particularly regarding whether the oath was binding in the first place. It reflects the broader Islamic principle that legal acts must be performed with the same formality as their inception.
